full_judgment:
18. Learned trial Judge on a proper discussion and consideration of the testimonies of P.W.1, P.W.4 and P.W.5 found contradictions inconsistencies and infirmities in their testimonies and recorded positive decision that plaintiff's story of Bainapatra was concocted one. Lower appellate Court found that plaintiff purchased the suit property by three registered deed dated 30.11.1954 and 1.12.1981 Exhibit I series followed by Bainapatra dated 15.2.1967 but the said Bainapatra had not been produced before the court. Lower appellate Court found contradiction between the testimonies of P.Ws. 1, 2 and 4 on the point of payment of earnest money. In spite of that it took the view that contradiction of P.W. 4 was not sufficient to turn down plaintiffs respondents claim. The approach made by lower appellate court on this point appeared to be purely wooden and the term of reasoning does not app to be intelligible. The appellate court held that probably in 1967 the vendors received Tk. 9800/-. Probability is always a probability and that cannot be proof. Lower appellate court did not appear to have adverted to the reasoned finding and decision reached by the trial court to the effect that plaintiff's story of Bainapatra was concocted one and the lower appellate court, thus, committed a substantial error in reversing the decisions rendered by trial court which rested on proper discussion, analysis assessment and consideration of testimonies of P.Ws. 1, 4-5. 

 28. Burden of Proof is the obligation to adduce evidence to the satisfaction of the court in order to establish the existence or non-existence of a fact contended by a party. The provision as to burden of proof is founded on the Rule i.e. incumbit probatio qui dicit non qui negat-the burden of proving a fact rests on the party who substantially assents the affirmative of the issue and not upon the party who denies it, for a negative is usually incapable of proof. This Rule is derived from Roman Law and is supportable not only on the ground of fairness but also upon that of the greater practical difficulty which is invilued in proving a negative that in proving on affirmative. The plaintiff failed to discharge the burden of proof that there had been an amicable arrangement amongst the Cadastral Survey recorded tenants and the suit property fell in the share of Hasen Sk.
